metaDescription: Electrolux cordless stick vacuums from WellQ7 to Ultimate800 compared by nozzle sets, filtration, weight and pet tools, so you match the tier to your floors.
expertTake: The Electrolux Ultimate800 Complete Home is the most capable stick in the family, with four nozzles and a blade that cuts hair off the roller. The WellQ7 is the value pick, keeping the cyclonic bin and the five-step filter at a lower tier. Skip these if you want a sealed allergy system with a published seal claim; the filtration here is multi-step but not described as sealed.
introParagraphs: This maker sells its cordless sticks in tiers that differ less in raw power than in nozzles, bin size and hair handling. Knowing which tier you need saves buying a nozzle set you will never use or missing the one you do.

The decision comes down to floors and pets. A hard-floor home wants a roller nozzle designed for bare boards, a pet home wants a motorized pet nozzle and a hair-cutting blade, and a mixed home wants a set that covers both without swapping parts.

products.name: Electrolux Ultimate800 Complete Home stick, four nozzles

specList.label: Hair
specList.value: BrushRoll Clean blade cuts hairs and fibers

products.description:
The Ultimate800 is the top of the family, and the set of four nozzles is the reason. One designed for hard floors, one for multi-surface use, one for pet hair and one for tight spots mean the stick changes to suit each job instead of compromising on one head. The BrushRoll Clean blade cuts hair and fibers that wind on the bristle nozzle, which solves the problem that makes bristle sticks a chore.

The five-step filtration system pairs with an integrated cyclonic design, so dirt is separated before it reaches the filters. Compared with the Ultimate700 it adds nozzles and the blade, and compared with the WellQ7 it is lighter and newer. The cost is complexity: more nozzles means more parts to store and clean.

Ownership is mostly nozzle care. Rinse the washable filters on the manual's schedule, run the blade-cleaning action now and then and keep the nozzles in a bag on the dock so none goes missing. Electrolux sells batteries and filters for the line, so the pack is a repair, not a replacement. When you switch nozzles, release the latch on the wand with the motor off, and set the unused nozzle on the dock so its bristles are not crushed, since a flattened bristle strip on the bare-floor nozzle leaves a faint streak where it no longer meets the floor evenly. Keep the small crevice tool in the same bag.
products.bestFor: Mixed floors and pets that want a nozzle for every job.
pros: BrushRoll Clean blade cuts hair off the roller
cons: More nozzles to store and clean
Costs more than the lower tiers
Filtration is not described as sealed

products.name: Electrolux Ultimate700 stick, PowerPro nozzle, 50 min

specList.label: Nozzle
specList.value: PowerPro bristle nozzle with LED lights

products.description:
At under five pounds the Ultimate700 is the lightest stick in the family, and the PowerPro bristle nozzle with LED lights highlights fine dust on hard floors as well as carpet. A full-tilt design lets the head recline to reach under furniture without kneeling.

The maker states that the five-step filtration traps 99 percent of particles as small as 0.3 microns, a manufacturer claim that describes the filter chain and should not be read as proof of a sealed system. The fifty minute figure is the maker's rating, so expect less on carpet.

Next to the Ultimate600 it is lighter and has a smaller bin, so it suits a flat better than a house. Rinse the filter on schedule, clear the bristle nozzle of hair and confirm the replacement pack listing before relying on the stick for many years. Because it is so light, it tips easily when parked, so use the dock or a stand and do not lean it on a table edge, and when you carry it upstairs hold the wand near the motor rather than at the handle, which cuts the lever effect and keeps the head from swinging into a wall.
products.bestFor: Smaller homes and users who want the lightest stick.
pros: Under five pounds, light on the wrist
cons: Filtration claim is not a sealed-system claim

products.name: Electrolux Ultimate600 Complete Home with 3 nozzles

specList.label: Filtration
specList.value: 5-step, 99.94 percent of dirt claimed inside the chamber

products.description:
The Ultimate600 Complete Home gives you three specialized nozzles for multi-surface, hard-floor and pet work, which is the sensible set for a mixed household. A detachable hand unit and a large bin round it out, and the stick weighs under six pounds.

The 99.94 percent figure is the maker's description of how much dirt the filtration keeps inside the chamber, not a measure of what reaches your room air. Against the Ultimate800 it has one fewer nozzle and no hair-cutting blade, but it gives you the specialized nozzles at a lower tier.

Store the three nozzles with the dock, rinse the filters and empty the bin at the line. Because a larger bin carries more weight when full, empty it a little early, and confirm the pack listing. The pet nozzle in the set suits fur on a sofa as well as on the floor, so use it with the hand unit attached, working in short strokes with the nap, and use the multi-surface nozzle for rugs where the pet nozzle's stiffer bristles may be too aggressive for a loose weave or a fringe.
products.bestFor: Mixed homes that want specialized nozzles at a mid tier.
pros: Large bin and detachable hand unit
cons: Filtration claim is a maker figure

products.name: Electrolux WellQ7 cordless 2-in-1, 5-step filter, 50 min
products.description:
The WellQ7 is the base of the modern family: a motorized bristle nozzle for carpet, hardwood and rugs, axial cyclonic separation to throw dirt out of the airflow and a five-step filter. The 2-in-1 design lets the hand unit come off for stairs and upholstery.

Compared with the Ultimate series it is a plainer and slightly heavier machine, with fewer nozzles and no blade. That is what makes it the value pick for someone who wants a cyclonic stick without paying for the extras.

Empty the bin at the line, rinse the washable filters and clear the bristle nozzle of hair. A bristle roller wraps long hair, so keep scissors near the stand, and confirm the battery listing for the WellQ7 platform. The cyclonic bin works best when it is emptied before the dirt reaches the filter shroud, so treat the fill line as a firm limit, and rinse the shroud every few months, because a film of fine dust on it reduces the separation that makes the cyclonic design worthwhile in the first place.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a cyclonic stick without extra nozzles.
pros: Axial cyclonic separation keeps the filter clean
Hand unit for stairs and upholstery
cons: Fewer nozzles than the Ultimate tiers

products.badge: Best Pet Nozzle at the Base Tier
products.name: Electrolux WellQ7 Pet 2-in-1 with PetPro+ nozzle
products.description:
Electrolux builds the Pet version around a motorized PetPro+ nozzle designed to lift pet hair, with the same cyclonic bin and five-step filter as the base WellQ7. For a house with a shedding dog it is the simplest upgrade from the standard nozzle.

Compared with the Ultimate800 it has one nozzle instead of four and no hair-cutting blade, so hair still needs occasional cutting. Compared with the standard WellQ7 it trades a general nozzle for a pet-specific one.

Empty the bin before it packs, rinse the washable parts and check the PetPro+ nozzle for hair at the ends. The hand unit is useful for sofas and car seats. A single pet nozzle serves both rugs and sofa fabric, but it is not a hard-floor nozzle, so on bare boards use the lower setting to avoid flicking crumbs, and consider adding the separate hard-floor nozzle if your home has more wood than carpet, since the pet nozzle's stiffer bristles are the wrong tool for polished planks.
products.bestFor: Pet households that want a pet-specific nozzle at a lower tier.
pros: Motorized PetPro+ nozzle for pet hair
cons: Only one nozzle in the box

products.name: Electrolux Ergorapido Pet 2-in-1, 48 min, EasySteer
products.description:
The Ergorapido is the older design in the family, and its signature is the 180 degree EasySteer head that swivels around furniture and chair legs. It carries a motorized pet nozzle and a BrushRoll Clean feature that cuts fibers from the roller.

The 48 minute figure is the maker's rating and slightly shorter than the newer 50 minute lines. Against the WellQ7 Pet it has the better steering and the hair-cutting feature but is older, so confirm that parts and batteries are still sold.

Empty the bin, rinse the filters and check the nozzle. The 2-in-1 hand unit handles couch cushions and car interiors, and the older body is a reminder to confirm the battery listing before you buy. The swiveling head is a mixed blessing: it follows furniture beautifully, but the pivot collects hair and thread, so open it up every month and clear the joint with a small brush, since a stiff pivot undoes the very steering advantage that makes this model worth considering.
products.bestFor: Furniture-heavy rooms where steering matters more than newer features.
pros: BrushRoll Clean cuts fibers from the roller
Hand unit for couches and cars

buyingCriteria.explanation: The Ultimate800 includes four nozzles and the Ultimate600 Complete Home three, while the WellQ7 and Ultimate700 ship with one motorized bristle nozzle. Specialized nozzles for hard floor and pets matter more than a larger motor. Count what is in the box, and check whether the extra nozzles are included in the listing you are viewing, because the same model number is often sold both as a single-nozzle stick and as a complete set at a higher tier, and the difference is easy to miss in the product photos.

The Ultimate800 and Ergorapido Pet use BrushRoll Clean to cut fibers off the roller, while the WellQ7 bristle nozzle wraps long hair. Hair wrap is the chore that decides whether a stick gets used. Pick the blade if you have long-haired pets, and remember that the blade reduces wrap on the roller but does not catch strands that slip past to the bearing ends, so a quick look at the nozzle every few weeks is still part of owning any bristle-roller stick, even this one.

The Ultimate700 is under five pounds and the Ultimate600 under six, while the WellQ7 is heavier. A full-tilt head reaches under furniture without kneeling. Light weight matters most to users who find a heavier stick tiring, and a tilting head matters most in a home with low sofas and beds, where a rigid wand forces you to crouch, so weigh these two features together when you compare tiers.

The family quotes figures such as 99 percent at 0.3 micron and 99.94 percent of dirt kept in the chamber. These are maker figures for the filter chain, not a sealed-system rating. If allergies are a concern, treat them as a good filter, not a guarantee, empty the bin outdoors and wash the filters on schedule, and consider a sealed model from another maker if a household member has asthma that is triggered by fine dust.

The Ultimate600 lists a larger dust bin, while the Ultimate700 is smaller. A larger bin means fewer stops in a house with shedding pets. The trade is weight when it is full, so a user with a weak wrist may prefer a smaller bin emptied more often, and a large bin is best matched to a person who vacuums a whole floor in one go and wants no mid-room stops.

Electrolux sells batteries and filters for the current lines, but older designs like the Ergorapido deserve a check. A removable pack and a listing for the exact model number decide the machine's lifespan.

cards.label: Ultimate series
cards.text: The Ultimate600, 700 and 800 are lighter, with PowerPro nozzles and, on the 800, a hair-cutting blade. They cost more.

cards.label: WellQ7 series
cards.text: The WellQ7 and WellQ7 Pet are heavier and simpler, with cyclonic bins and bristle or pet nozzles. They suit buyers who want a basic stick.

howToChoose.note: Ultimate for pets and mixed floors, WellQ7 for value.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A set that includes a hard-floor nozzle and a multi-surface nozzle, and a full-tilt head. Store the extra nozzles with the dock.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have long-haired pets or mixed floors. The Ultimate800's blade and nozzle set remove the daily hair chore.

cards.label: Save if

faq.a: The Ultimate800 Complete Home has the most nozzles and the hair-cutting blade. The WellQ7 is the better value, because it keeps the cyclonic bin and the five-step filter that define the family and leaves out only the extra nozzles and the blade that many households never miss.
It cuts hair and fibers off the roller as it spins. It reduces cutting by hand, but you should still check the roller.
